Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of
low back pain and muscle spasm. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the
forces expected in a collision of this type. Over the course of ten visits, care
included physical therapy, manual therapy, home exercise instruction, and
anti-inflammatory medication as needed. The duration of treatment ran somewhat longer
than is typical for a uncomplicated lumbar strain, and progress was gradual but
steady. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm the presence of a
lumbar soft tissue injury consistent with the reported incident. No prior injury to
the lumbar region is known from the patient's hitsory or available records. Billing
review of two similar charges recorded on the same date of service is currently in
progress. At discharge, the patient had improved in range of motion and pain levels but
still reported intermittent discomfort with prolonged sitting. Continued home exercise
and follow-up as needed were recommended.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
